newsitem.title: GERMANY: EARLY NORTH GERMAN WHEAT YIELDS REACH 7-10 TONNES.
newsitem.headline: EARLY NORTH GERMAN WHEAT YIELDS REACH 7-10 TONNES.

text.p: Wheat yields in Germany's most northerly state of Schleswig-Holstein are between seven and 10 tonnes per hectare, the local agriculture chamber said.
That compared with 7.32 tonnes in 1996, when the state harvested 1.43 million tonnes of winter wheat and 7,400 tonnes of spring wheat.
A statement from the chamber said 10 percent of wheat had been harvested in Schleswig-Holstein and farmers were optimistic about yields.
But it was too early to generalise on protein contents and falling numbers.
Prices were around 240 marks a tonne.
This year's area is 175,747 hectares for winter wheat and 2,457 for spring wheat.
Harvesting of barley, rye and rapeseed was due to be completed this week, with good quality reported so far.
Oats and triticale were also benefiting from sunny harvest weather, which meant drying was no longer necessary.
